figures_added.what: Big-wheel figure for the opener: ground line, two support legs, wheel circle (soft blue fill-opacity 0.18), centre dot labelled 'centre 30 m', a dashed radius up to a car labelled '25 m', and a second car at the side. Theme-safe: all strokes/text use currentColor, region fills use fill-opacity. viewBox + role=img + aria-label, no external refs. Numbers match the opener boxes (low 5 m = 30-25, high 55 m = 30+25).

Chart.js y = sin x over 0..360 (25 points, tension 0.35). Every plotted point satisfies y = sin(x). Makes the three x-axis crossings (0, 180, 360) visible for the 'how many crossings?' question (answer 3).
Chart.js y = cos x over 0..360. Points satisfy y = cos(x). The curve crosses the x-axis at 90 and 270, supporting 'solve cos x = 0, give the first value' (answer 90).
Chart.js y = cos x plus a dashed horizontal line y = 0.5. The line cuts the cosine curve twice (at 60 and 300), making the count concrete for 'how many solutions does cos x = 0.5 have?' (answer 2).
Chart.js y = sin x plus a dashed horizontal line y = 0.5. The line meets the sine curve at 30 and 150, the two solutions of sin x = 0.5; supports 'give the larger solution' (answer 150).

notes: Figures added in the same pass as the guided conversion. Charts use the house schema (type scatter, line datasets, tension 0.35, curve #3b82f6, dashed grey #9ca3af reference line, x ticks stepSize 90, y range -1.2..1.2). Every curve point was regenerated programmatically from math.sin/math.cos and re-verified against its equation (0 mismatches). Tangent problems deliberately have no chart because the 90/270 asymptotes make a clean Chart.js render awkward; sine/cosine charts cover the questions where a figure genuinely helps. Opener claim of a big wheel is now backed by an inline SVG per the show-what-you-say rule.
